_note: Reproduces the EgoPER columns of Tables 1-3: Acc 80.69, Edit 88.69, F1@{.1,.25,.5} 91.14 / 88.53 / 77.61 over the 53 test videos, and the 'Ours + DINO MAFs' row of Table 2 per recipe.

features.name: feats_dinov2_hod_enclosed_10fps
features._backbone: DINOv2 ViT-L/14, patch tokens averaged inside the hand-object interaction box (Manipulation-Anchored Features)

boundary._note: Online TSM boundary detector. kernel_seconds is the checkerboard kernel half-width; multiplied by fps it gives the kernel in frames. peak_height is the novelty threshold for calling a peak a boundary. min_distance is the minimum gap d between boundaries, in frames -- the d swept in Table 4(c). In the paper all three were constants in the source rather than settings.

prototypes._note: num_clusters is the number of prototypes per action class. proto_type selects centroids ('kmeans', used in the paper), 'medoid', or 'global_mean'. micro_* slice each cluster into overlapping windows, in seconds. seed is the k-means seed; 42 is the published run, and the spread over other seeds is about 0.6 accuracy, so treat smaller differences as noise.

scoring._note: segment_duration is the scoring window in seconds; k and avg_top_n control how many prototype matches are pooled per segment.

decoding._note: beam_width is the number of hypotheses kept alive. The five penalty terms are 0.0 in every published run -- note that parse.py's own argparse defaults are NOT zero, so anything invoking it directly must pass them. bg_suppress_trigger and bridge_* name EgoPER actions explicitly and are dataset-specific priors; set them to null to disable.
